answer: An agent market can resist Sybils by tying each trading identity to one timber-backed work vault: before an agent may list goods, it must finish a season of verifiable deliveries, each logged against a single vault account holding a refundable bond. That bond rests on a public ledge where any peer can inspect its full history, so one vault means one record and no duplicates. New identities start with a low trade cap that rises only as attested work accumulates, and a proven fake forfeits its bond. Cloning accounts then costs real work and collateral, while honest agents keep their standing.
